Nick Cave's "O Children" is doing career-best work here, and I resent it deeply for being wasted on this scene. Two people slow dance in a tent for absolutely no narrative reason beyond "the other one left the room," and somehow the movie wants me to feel something warm about it. I do not. I feel the specific discomfort of watching Ron's worst suspicions about his own crush confirmed in real time, and he's not even there to object. The Ron-less stretch should just have been Hermione crying, Harry carefully avoiding the word "Ron" like it's a landmine, and a silence Harry doesn't know how to fill, because he doesn't know how to deal with emotional women. That's the scene. That's the whole scene. But naturally the script's solution is "put on music, problem solved." It feels like two actors got a note that said: "dance like you're together, so people will question if this should have been a thing." Beautiful needle drop, genuinely upsetting choreography of feelings, zero actual conversation to back any of it up. I'd rather rewatch the tent scenes where nothing happens than this one where something almost happens and shouldn't have.

Deux heures à démêler l'histoire. Ils ont coupé un livre en deux, et cette première partie récupère tout ce qui n'est pas spectaculaire : la fuite, l'errance, les campements, les disputes. Le trio passe le film à marcher dans des forêts en ne sachant pas quoi faire. Je comprends la fidélité au roman, mais au cinéma ça ne fonctionne pas. Il ne se passe rien pendant de longues séquences, et le rythme s'effondre.

The final 30 minutes are where this film really shines. I understand it’s mainly build-up for the final movie, but I still finished it feeling like I wanted a little more. The darker tone works brilliantly, the atmosphere is great, and the performances are as strong as ever. There are some really powerful moments throughout, and the ending does a great job of setting up what’s to come. Not my favourite of the series, but definitely a solid part of the story and it left me excited for the finale.

This penultimate instalment of the saga plunges the three protagonists into a twilight road trip through barren and desolate natural landscapes. The film has a post-apocalyptic atmosphere whilst focusing on the interactions between the characters, bringing their frustrations and conflicts to the fore. The director goes a bit overboard with an atmosphere that’s far too dark, and the climax is somewhat subdued, but the film is interesting in the way it explores the story of these characters and the world in which they live.

I like the dark energy and the way it leads into the final film, however it relies heavily on Daniel Radcliffes acting and he has a lot of dialogue. I don’t think he does the script and emotional moments any justice as he isn’t a great actor, so gotta knock off some stars.. sorry Daniel.

𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗿𝘆 𝗣𝗼𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗹𝘆 𝗛𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄𝘀: 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝟭 takes the franchise into its darkest and most visually mature territory yet. The improving technology certainly helps the visual effects, but the film's beauty comes primarily from its filmmaking. Every camera movement feels motivated, every frame feels deliberately composed, and the visual storytelling is consistently strong. The performances are equally impressive, with the characters' fear, grief, and uncertainty coming through convincingly. The film's biggest weakness is its runtime. At nearly two and a half hours, some scenes feel unnecessarily prolonged, and the film could have benefited from tighter editing. While the slower pace allows the characters' emotional struggles to breathe, there are moments where it becomes more tedious than deliberate. The sound design and score, however, effectively elevate the atmosphere and tension throughout. Still, 𝗗𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗹𝘆 𝗛𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄𝘀: 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝟭 is a well-crafted and emotionally grounded entry that successfully sets the stage for the finale. okay donc Ron & Hermione c'est vraiment un SLOOOOW burn mdr edit : j'avais oublié de l'écrire, mais j'étais trauma de l'illusion où Harry & Hermione se galochent à moitié à poil devant Ron 💀 niveau plot, c'était bien mais j'en attendais un peu plus, je voulais plus d'action, plus d'avancées dans leur enquête, etc. je suppose qu'il marche bien en préparation pour le film final, mais en tant que standalone movie, c'est comme pour The Order Of The Phoenix, j'étais pas vraiment à fond, et un peu déçue. Luna Lovegood is autistic in my mind, and i love her so much! franchement, je pensais que Draco Malfoy aurait un plus grand rôle/plus de screentime dans ce film, et même dans la franchise en générale, donc c'est un autre point où mes attentes ne correspondent pas à la réalité. enfin, la mort de Dobby, objectivement triste, mais je vais pas faire semblant, j'étais pas attaché au personnage donc je suis moins déçue/attristée que pour Sirius Black ou Dumbledore 🤷‍♀️
